what_the_selective_counts_do_and_do_not_.shows: R_theta CAN expose selective chemistry: the fixed arm found 134 and 178 selective molecules out of 300 charged, drawn from R_theta fibers.
what_the_selective_counts_do_and_do_not_.does_NOT_show: that selective candidates were present in every fiber the ADAPTIVE arm actually saw. The arms visit different states once they diverge, so this does not rule out proposal availability as a local factor for the adaptive arm.
what_the_selective_counts_do_and_do_not_.status_of_zero_selective_under_adaptive: a DIAGNOSTIC CHARACTERIZATION, not a failure criterion. The official benchmark does not require preferring selectivity over higher-HV promiscuous points.

why_diagnosis_from_existing_artifacts.method: no new evaluations. Recomputed each arm's HV lift with and without its single highest-JNK3 new molecule, counted new molecules on the final front, and counted how many of those individually carry >0.1% of total HV (leave-one-out).
why_diagnosis_from_existing_artifacts.reading: CAUTION. Adaptive's large seed-101 win -- the one that carries the mean -- is 60.6% attributable to a SINGLE molecule. Its other two seeds lift +0.036 and +0.032, against the fixed arm's +0.045 and +0.032. And while adaptive puts comparably many new molecules on the front (78-101 vs 53-74), almost none of them are individually load-bearing (0-7 carry >0.1% of HV, against 74 for fixed on seed 101), which is the signature of a clustered, mutually-redundant front rather than gains spread across several nondominated regions.
why_diagnosis_from_existing_artifacts.verdict_on_the_richer_story: This looks like ONE LUCKY HIGH-JNK3 POINT more than broad improvement across multiple nondominated regions. It counts for official HV, but it does NOT yet support the adaptive-Pareto-navigation story.
